name: Adora Cheung
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Multiple sources place her birth around June 1983 (UK Companies House; age 30 in an August 2013 Mercury News profile). YC S10 / Pathjoy–Homejoy work began around 2010 at about age 27; Homejoy’s major $38M raise and multi-city scale came in 2013 (~age 30).
early_history_summary: Grew up in a small South Carolina town; earned a CS bachelor’s at Clemson and an economics master’s at Rochester, then left a PhD path for Silicon Valley product work (including Slide.com) before co-founding Pathjoy/Homejoy with her brother via Y Combinator.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond growing up in a small South Carolina town; later co-founded with her brother Aaron.
evidence_summary: Contemporary press listed Cheung as age 30 in August 2013 and UK company filings list date of birth June 1983, which places YC S10 and Homejoy founding after age 26. Homejoy later raised tens of millions and expanded widely, then shut down in 2015 amid contractor lawsuits and unit-economics issues; Cheung later became a YC partner and co-founded Instalab.

name: Martin Lorentzon
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Born April 1, 1969; first major founding (Netstrategy/Tradedoubler with Felix Hagnö) was September 1999 at age 30; Spotify co-founding with Daniel Ek was 2006 at age 37.
early_history_summary: Born in Småland, Sweden, to a teacher mother and economist father; studied industrial economics at Chalmers and other Swedish business schools; interned at Telia (1995) and worked in Silicon Valley at AltaVista and Cell Ventures before entrepreneurship in his thirties.
family_context_summary: Mother Brita was a teacher; father Sven was an economist; two older siblings; family moved to Borås when he was an infant.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were professionals (teacher and economist) but not documented as tech-domain specialists.
evidence_summary: Lorentzon’s documented breakout entrepreneurship (Tradedoubler 1999; Spotify 2006) occurred well after age 26. Earlier years were education and corporate/tech employment (Telia, AltaVista, Cell Ventures). Later outcomes include Tradedoubler success and multi-billion Spotify stake, but those milestones are post-26.

name: Llion Jones
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. North Wales Chronicle (Nov 2018) described him as 34, implying birth ~1984; MSc Advanced Computer Science (University of Birmingham) around 2009 (~age 25) is ordinary academic progress. Seminal co-authorship of “Attention Is All You Need” (2017) and Sakana AI co-founding (2023) occurred in his thirties.
early_history_summary: Born and raised in Bangor/Gwynedd, Wales; learned programming young; studied AI and computer science at the University of Birmingham (BSc then MSc ~2009); later joined Google (YouTube then research) and co-authored the Transformer paper in 2017.
evidence_summary: Jones’s field-defining work (Transformer, 2017) and later Sakana AI co-founding occurred after age 26 given a ~1984 birth year. Early path shows strong interest in computing and solid university training but no independently verified breakout product, paper, or company by 26.

name: Paul Buchheit
milestone_by_age_26: Created Gmail at Google and launched it publicly on April 1, 2004 at age 26 (born Nov 7, 1977); as Google employee #23 he had begun the project around 2001 and also prototyped what became AdSense and popularized the “Don’t be evil” motto.
early_history_summary: Born in Webster, New York; studied computer engineering at Case Western Reserve University and rowed crew; worked at Intel, then joined Google in 1999 as roughly the 23rd employee. He spent Google’s early years building Gmail’s search-and-storage model and related ads prototypes before the 2004 invite-only launch that redefined consumer webmail.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond birthplace in Webster, New York.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Google early employee, Silicon Valley, Case Western, Gmail, AdSense prototype
evidence_summary: Buchheit joined Google in 1999 at about age 21 and by 2001 was building Gmail, shipping a product that launched in 2004 when he was 26 and became a defining consumer internet service. Advantages were primarily immersion in early Google’s talent density and infrastructure rather than documented family capital or inherited networks. Later path includes FriendFeed, Facebook acquisition, Y Combinator partnership, and active angel investing.
starting_point: Born November 7, 1977, in Webster, New York; studied computer engineering at Case Western Reserve University; family details not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Angel investor and longtime Y Combinator partner; creator of Gmail and early AdSense prototype; previously co-founded FriendFeed (acquired by Facebook).

trajectory.event: Joined Google as roughly employee #23 after a stint at Intel, entering the early search-startup ecosystem.
Began developing Gmail at Google, focusing on search-driven webmail with large free storage.
Publicly launched Gmail (April 1), establishing a new standard for consumer email and related ad tech prototypes.
Left Google and co-founded FriendFeed with Bret Taylor and others.
FriendFeed was acquired by Facebook, and he became a Facebook employee briefly.
Left Facebook to become a partner at Y Combinator while continuing personal angel investing.
Won The Economist innovation award in computing and telecommunications for his work.

name: Brian Leroux
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Batch lists birth year 1979; PhoneGap originated at Nitobi’s iPhoneDevCamp work in August 2008 (~age 28–29). Leadership of PhoneGap/Apache Cordova at Adobe and later Begin.com founding came later; no earlier dated breakout verified.
early_history_summary: Canadian software developer associated with Nitobi Software; early contributor and later leader of the PhoneGap open-source project (Apache Cordova after Adobe’s 2011 Nitobi acquisition); later co-founded Begin.com and has worked at Adobe and Sanity.
evidence_summary: PhoneGap’s documented origin is 2008 at Nitobi, which—if birth year 1979 is correct—is after age 26. Public materials emphasize his PhoneGap/Cordova leadership and later serverless/FWA work, not a pre-26 material milestone with dual-source dating.

name: Joshua Bloch
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Born August 28, 1961; CMU PhD thesis completed May 1990 at age 28; major public impact (Java Collections Framework leadership, Effective Java 2001 Jolt Award, Google Chief Java Architect from 2004) came in his thirties and later.
early_history_summary: Earned a Columbia CS bachelor’s and a Carnegie Mellon PhD (1990 thesis on replication of abstract data objects, ACM Distinguished Doctoral Dissertation Award nominee); later Senior Systems Designer at Transarc, Distinguished Engineer at Sun, then Chief Java Architect at Google.
evidence_summary: Bloch’s career is highly distinguished in Java platform design and API pedagogy, but the dated milestones that made him widely known (Effective Java, Collections Framework leadership, Google role) are after age 26. His PhD finished at 28.

name: Chandrajit Bajaj
category: Computer scientist / computational geometry and visualization
milestone_by_age_26: Completed a Cornell PhD in computer science in 1984 under John E. Hopcroft (after a 1983 master’s) and began a Purdue University computer science faculty position the same year, at approximately age 26 (born 1958; BTech IIT Delhi 1980).
early_history_summary: Born in Calcutta, India (1958); earned a BTech from IIT Delhi (1980), then MS (1983) and PhD (1984) at Cornell under Hopcroft. He moved immediately into the professoriate at Purdue (1984–1997), building a research career in geometric modeling, visualization, and computational biology before later joining UT Austin.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources beyond birthplace in Calcutta, India.
primary_early_advantage_tags: IIT Delhi, Cornell, Hopcroft advisor, Purdue faculty, computational geometry
evidence_summary: Bajaj’s age-26 milestone is elite academic pipeline completion: IIT Delhi undergraduate training, Cornell graduate work under Hopcroft, and an immediate U.S. research faculty role. Later career includes long UT Austin leadership of the Computational Visualization Center and ACM/AAAS fellowships; early advantages are institutional rather than family-capital based on reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born 1958 in Calcutta, India; family background not documented in reviewed sources; entered the IIT Delhi pipeline before U.S. graduate study.
current_position: Professor of computer science at the University of Texas at Austin; Computational Applied Mathematics Chair in Visualization and director of the Computational Visualization Center; ACM and AAAS Fellow.

trajectory.event: Received BTech in computer science from IIT Delhi.
Completed master’s degree in computer science at Cornell University.
Completed Cornell PhD under John Hopcroft and joined Purdue University’s computer science faculty.
Moved to UT Austin as professor and visualization chair, later directing the Computational Visualization Center.
Elected AAAS Fellow for contributions spanning geometry, graphics, and scientific computing.
Named ACM Fellow.

name: Chris Barton
milestone_by_age_26: No confirmed birth year found in reviewed sources, so age at Shazam conception (1999) and co-founding (2000) cannot be verified; Wikipedia explicitly lists year of birth missing. Without age confirmation, a material ≤26 milestone cannot be established.
early_history_summary: Son of university professors (nuclear physics father John P. Barton; computer science mother Claudia F. Barton); UC Berkeley BA and MBA plus Cambridge finance master’s; strategy consulting and Microsoft internship before co-founding Shazam in London and later roles at Google, Dropbox, and Guard Inc.
family_context_summary: Father British nuclear physics professor; mother French computer science professor; parents ran a nuclear physics consultancy he has cited as entrepreneurial inspiration; childhood dyslexia reported.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were university professors in nuclear physics and computer science; dual UK/France background facilitated living/working in the UK for Shazam.
evidence_summary: Barton’s Shazam founding is a major entrepreneurial story, but eligibility requires a verified age ≤26 at a dated milestone. No secondary source supplied a reliable birth year, so the case is coded ineligible pending age verification.

name: Matt Cohler
milestone_by_age_26: Joined LinkedIn’s founding team in 2003 as vice president and general manager (LinkedIn launched May 2003) at age 25–26 (born March 27, 1977), becoming CEO Reid Hoffman’s early operational right hand after McKinsey and China work.
early_history_summary: Born in New York City (1977); Yale B.A. in music with honors (class of 2001); worked in China and as a McKinsey analyst, then entered LinkedIn’s founding team in 2003. He later became one of Facebook’s earliest hires (often cited among the first five to seven employees) as VP of product management before joining Benchmark as its youngest general partner in 2008.
family_context_summary: Born in New York City; public genealogy notes father Jonas Robert Cohler Jr.; detailed family financial background not documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as a tech-domain family apprenticeship in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Yale, McKinsey, LinkedIn founding team, Hoffman network, Silicon Valley social graph
evidence_summary: By age 26 Cohler was already a founding-team executive at LinkedIn during the professional-network wave, after Yale and McKinsey credentials and a relationship with Reid Hoffman. Subsequent Facebook product leadership and Benchmark investments (Instagram, Dropbox, Asana, Uber, Tinder, etc.) compounded that early network-and-execution seat; family domain advantages are not clearly documented.
starting_point: Born March 27, 1977, in New York City; Yale music graduate (2001); early career via McKinsey and China work before Silicon Valley startups.
current_position: Owner of Oslo Holdings (from 2020); former Benchmark general partner who stepped back from new funds while retaining influence from major social/enterprise investments; board and endowment roles including San Francisco Symphony and Environmental Defense Fund.

trajectory.event: Graduated Yale with a music B.A. and entered management consulting at McKinsey after China experience.
Joined LinkedIn’s founding team as vice president and general manager under Reid Hoffman.
Joined Facebook as one of its earliest employees and later served as VP of product management.
Left Facebook to become the youngest general partner at Benchmark Capital.
Led Benchmark’s early investment in Instagram, which Facebook acquired for about $1B in 2012.
Announced a step-back from leading Benchmark’s next fund while remaining active on existing portfolio boards.
Founded Oslo Holdings to manage a broader personal investment portfolio.

name: Nikolai Mushegian
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded MakerDAO with Rune Christensen around 2015 (age 21–22; born March 28, 1993) and designed/built the Single-Collateral Dai stablecoin system that launched in December 2017 when he was 24.
early_history_summary: Born in Lexington, Kentucky, to Soviet-immigrant life-scientist parents; excelled academically and musically in Kansas high school; graduated Carnegie Mellon SCS (CS + math minor) in 2014; taught a student-led blockchain course and worked on BitShares before co-founding MakerDAO and related Ethereum tooling (DappHub, WETH contributions).
family_context_summary: Parents Arcady Mushegian and Irina Sorokina are life scientists who immigrated from the Soviet Union in 1991; Ukrainian, Armenian, and Russian ancestry; great-grandfather Tigran Mushegian was rector of Yerevan State University in the 1930s.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were research life scientists rather than blockchain practitioners; intellectual/academic household, not a crypto-domain apprenticeship.
primary_early_advantage_tags: CMU SCS, BitShares, Ethereum early, MakerDAO, co-founder Rune Christensen, open-source crypto
evidence_summary: Mushegian’s MakerDAO co-founding and Dai architecture work by his early twenties is dual-sourced (Wikipedia biography plus MakerDAO/CoinDesk and Devcon materials). Elite CMU training, intense early blockchain practice, and a high-trust technical partnership with Christensen mattered more than inherited crypto capital. He later co-authored Balancer’s white paper and co-founded RAI/RICO before dying in 2022 at age 29.
starting_point: Born March 28, 1993, in Lexington, Kentucky, to Soviet-immigrant life-scientist parents; raised with strong academic expectations and multi-instrument musical training.
current_position: Died October 28, 2022, at age 29 in San Juan, Puerto Rico; final work included RAI and RICO stablecoin projects after earlier MakerDAO, WETH, and Balancer contributions.

trajectory.event: Graduated Carnegie Mellon SCS and deepened work on BitShares / pre-Ethereum decentralized applications.
Co-founded MakerDAO with Rune Christensen and began building Dai’s collateralized stablecoin architecture; presented at Ethereum Devcon1.
Helped develop Wrapped Ether (WETH) and security-hardened smart-contract patterns after the DAO hack era.
Single-Collateral Dai system he designed launched as MakerDAO’s official Dai release.
Co-authored the Balancer white paper and donated substantial MKR value to CMU SCS fellowships.
Co-founded the RAI project, a free-floating crypto-backed stablecoin system.
Died after drowning near Condado Beach in San Juan, Puerto Rico; police reported no foul play.

early_history_summary: Iowa State University computer engineering graduate; co-author/architect associated with BIND 9; long affiliation with Internet Systems Consortium; sparse independent biography.
evidence_summary: Public record is too thin to establish birth year or age-dated early milestones. Infrastructure contributions to BIND 9 are notable for specialists, but eligibility requires a confirmed ≤26 dated material milestone.
